decisions.text: send notes to all other projects to adopt the best things

relayed: approved, each as a wow standard with a check where practical, after an assistant outage in a TS/Convex web app (18 hours of silent failure, 0 error rows, 0 alerts, 22 green deploys): 1. validator-derived types, no hand-written twin of a runtime validator, exact returns so the type check fails on drift (every Convex query/mutation/action declares returns), a lint guard for casts, any and builder bypasses, and a v.any() ratchet; 2. failures are never silent: every background job, scheduled function or action failure lands in the app's error log and the user sees a failure state; 3. post-deploy smoke: call the critical server paths once as a production test account and go red if one fails, report-only, credentials on the needs-isaac ledger; 4. key-path traffic alarm against the same hours last week, alerting a staff address on a drop to zero, its setup a ledger item; 5. a core-flow coverage list (covered / partly / not covered), refreshed from feedback, incidents and production errors, gaps as DAG nodes; 6. every production incident gets a short HTML postmortem (root cause, why checks missed it, prevention units as DAG nodes). Per stack: TS/Convex web apps vs Godot games.
